heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P requires a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gear upgrade alongside an enclosure to reliably print eSUN ePA-CF without rapid wear or severe warping. Operating within an 11 mm³/s volumetric flow limit restricts safe printing speeds to a maximum of 131 mm/s using standard layer heights.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP Glue Stick (or Magigoo PA) as a release agent and thermal barrier
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 11 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent severe under-extrusion and extruder grinding.
Set the Part Cooling Fan to 0% for the first 5 layers and cap normal printing fan speed at 20% to prevent rapid cooling delamination.
Add a 10 mm brim with a 0.0 mm brim-to-object gap to combat corner lifting on the open-frame P1P chassis.
Lower Outer Wall and Inner Wall speeds to 100-120 mm/s to ensure structural layer adhesion and a uniform carbon fiber surface finish.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe warping and corner detachment from the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Open-frame draft exposure and nylon crystalline shrinkage differential caused by excessive cooling
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install temporary enclosure panels or a pop-up tent on the P1P, apply Magigoo PA on the bed, and turn off the auxiliary fan entirely.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking, nozzle clogging, and inconsistent extrusion width
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Chopped carbon fiber particles eroding and clogging the stock stainless steel nozzle, or filament moisture expansion
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Upgrade to a 0.4mm or 0.6mm Bambu Hardened Steel complete hotend assembly and dry the filament spool at 80°C for 8-12 hours.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak interlayer bonding causing parts to snap cleanly along layer lines
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speed or hotend temperature dropping below the nylon polymer fusion threshold
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise hotend temperature to 280°C, set part cooling fan to a maximum of 10-15%, and disable the chamber exhaust/auxiliary fan.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN ePA-CF on the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: No, the carbon fiber fibers will rapidly abrade the stock stainless steel nozzle within a few hundred grams, enlarging the orifice and ruining dimensional accuracy. Upgrade to Bambu's Hardened Steel hotend and hardened extruder gears before printing.

faq.question: Can the P1P handle nylon warp without a heated enclosure?
faq.answer: Small parts may succeed with a 100°C bed and thick brim, but medium to large components will warp severely due to ambient drafts. Adding an aftermarket enclosure or tent kit is strongly advised.

faq.question: How should I dry and feed eSUN ePA-CF on the P1P?
faq.answer: Dry the spool in an active filament dryer at 80°C for at least 8 to 12 hours prior to printing, and print directly from a heated dry box to prevent ambient moisture uptake during printing.

faq.question: Can I feed eSUN ePA-CF through the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: While it can feed through the AMS, abrasive PA-CF prematurely wears down the standard plastic AMS funnels and internal PTFE tubing. If printing frequently, feed directly from an external dry box or upgrade to hardened AMS feeder funnels.
